non_goals: No change to the frozen 56 tasks, no-hint protocol, 1200 s per-task wall limit, tool set, prompt or policy text, or strict all-56 scoring with timeouts counted as failures.
No cancellation, backend interrupt, monkeypatch, duplicated backend execution, new tool, task-specific logic, or pre-dispatch behavior intervention.
No answer, hint, validator, held-out data, raw trace, task ID, message, result, raw argument, raw tool name, credential, or network access.
No second arm, sham run, probe run, or extra formal evaluation; the only extra observable is the in-run sidecar inertness check.
No claim that the last durable query caused the timeout, that any pre-dispatch guard would help, or that an unpaired strict-pass difference is causal.
nodes.statement: Under the fixed 56-task no-hint 1200 s protocol, G6 localized all 3 observed timeout failures to a unique in-flight database_query, but its reported elapsed distribution is aggregate: 50/71 eligible timeout-cohort steps in 0-120 s, 21/71 in greater than 120 through 600 s, 0/71 in greater than 600 through 1200 s, and 0 unknown. Thus every recorded pre-exec in that cohort started with at least 600 s remaining, but the packet does not identify whether each timeout's last durable query_db pre-exec was in the first 120 s or the later 120-600 s bucket. The blocked engineering attempt shows no uniform safe in-flight cancellation primitive, so G7 does not attempt cancellation. The bounded problem is whether one write-only, inert sidecar at the verified hook can assign exactly one elapsed bucket to each observed timeout's unique last durable query_db pre-exec, preserve unknown for unclassifiable cases, and report per-cohort coverage without changing agent behavior or scoring. This is a diagnostic question about when the in-flight query started, not a claim that any query caused the timeout or that any score can improve.

nodes.falsification_condition: Contradicted if any observed timeout is timeout-negative, if the sidecar persists prohibited content, or if the sidecar changes agent-visible input, dispatch, results, or scoring. The early-start subclaim is contradicted if every observed timeout is timeout-positive, at least one is query_db-timeout-positive, and no query_db-timeout-positive task has elapsed_bucket 0_120. Inconclusive, not falsified, if no timeout occurs, any observed timeout is timeout-unknown, no query_db timeout occurs, non-timeout cohort coverage is below 0.8, or a required clock-derived bucket is unknown. A strict-pass difference alone neither supports nor falsifies the hypothesis.
nodes.possible_counterexample: Every timeout's last durable query_db pre-exec may be in the greater-than-120-through-600 s bucket, so no early-start timeout exists. The timeout may be caused by a harness kill, resource exhaustion, or an uninterruptible call rather than by query start time. The query may have started early but still not be causal. A timeout may leave no durable pre-exec record, making the last-event class unknown. The three-timeout sample is small, and a single unpaired run may not reproduce the G6 pattern.
nodes.prediction: In one formal 56-task no-hint run with the fixed 1200 s limit and strict all-56 scoring with timeouts as failures: (1) known-strict-fail, strict-pass, and strict-verdict-unknown cohorts each reach at least 0.8 complete-task sidecar coverage, where covered means every eligible step has exactly one pre-exec record and one matching post_exec_finished record at the same ordinal with a non-unknown coarse tool class; (2) if at least one timeout occurs, every observed timeout receives exactly one non-unknown last-event coarse tool class and exactly one non-unknown elapsed bucket; (3) at least one observed timeout has a last durable query_db pre-exec in the 0-120 s bucket; (4) the strict-pass partition is reported descriptively with no predicted increase; and (5) enabling versus disabling the sidecar produces identical control flow, return values, messages, dispatch, results, and scoring.
nodes.statement: In a new child of the verified g006 code parent, a write-only sidecar at DataAgentWithSelfObservation._handle_tool_call will classify each observed timeout's unique last durable unresolved pre-exec as database_query, other, or unknown, and assign its validated elapsed at that pre-exec to 0-120 s, greater than 120 through 600 s, greater than 600 through 1200 s, or unknown. At least one observed timeout will have a last durable query_db pre-exec in the 0-120 s bucket, indicating a query launched within the first 120 s and still in flight at the 1200 s wall limit; every observed timeout will be classifiable without an unknown last-event elapsed bucket. The sidecar will not change agent-visible inputs, dispatch, results, or scoring.

engineering_acceptance_criteria: The code parent is executable and resolves to the bound g006 tree 845e0f89f3df104d1fcb0ca564256fe8ca0f92c8880127dc4b3c2d4cfb0244c6; launch is blocked otherwise.

The runtime hook is exactly DataAgentWithSelfObservation._handle_tool_call, with pre-exec observation before tool dispatch and post_exec_finished observation in a finally block that re-raises unchanged.

The execution source-field allowlist is only tool_name, hook-local ordinal, hook-local monotonic clock, DAB_TASK_DEADLINE_MONOTONIC, DAB_TASK_SPAWN_REMAINING_SEC, the fixed 1200 s protocol limit, and anonymous_task_index; parsed_tool_args are not read or persisted by this sidecar.
Static data-flow review and hook-local tests prove the sink is write-only, non-blocking, not fed to the agent, and does not mutate arguments, dispatch, results, or scoring.
Enabled and disabled sidecar paths produce identical control flow, return values, messages, dispatch, results, and scoring in prelaunch tests.
The exact frozen protocol is bound: 56 no-hint tasks, 1200 seconds per task, strict pass over all 56, timeouts counted as failures, and one formal run only.

The sidecar schema accepts only anonymous_task_index, hook_local_step_ordinal, event_phase, coarse_tool_class, elapsed_bucket, completion_boolean, sidecar_terminal_status, and coverage_status, plus aggregate counts in an optional task-end summary.
Coverage below 0.8 per non-timeout cohort is reported as Evidence and does not veto launch.
All outputs preserve unknown categories and avoid causal or strict-gain claims.
nodes.expected_behavior: The agent and evaluator behave as in the bound g006 parent, while the sidecar appends anonymous structural records and a per-task last-event elapsed bucket. No strict-pass gain is expected from instrumentation. For each observed timeout, the unique last durable pre-exec is classified into one elapsed bucket or unknown. Missing, unmatched, or clock-invalid records remain unknown rather than being imputed.
nodes.frozen_evaluation: Exactly one formal candidate evaluation over the same frozen 56 no-hint tasks, the same single 1200 s per-task wall limit, the same harness and evidence-integrity binding, and strict pass over all 56 tasks with timeouts counted as failures. No task is added, removed, re-scored, or reinterpreted; no partial-log content overrides a timeout verdict; no held-out data or prior graph is consulted; no second arm, sham run, or probe run is added. The child's partition and per-timeout last-event buckets are compared descriptively with the G6 partition of 37 strict pass, 13 known strict fail, 3 strict-verdict unknown, and 3 timeout failures. Because this is one unpaired diagnostic run over a small timeout count, any difference is reported as a small-count observation and not as an established causal effect.
nodes.implementation_scope: One hook-local sidecar in a new g006-derived child: one durable pre-exec append and one durable post_exec_finished append per hook invocation, plus an optional best-effort task-end summary. The fixed tool-class mapping and elapsed-bucket mapping must be declared before launch. The source-field allowlist and post-exec completion boundary must be confirmed in the bound parent before implementation; if completion cannot be observed without reading tool results, messages, or task content, do not launch. No new tool, task, prompt, policy sentence, timing limit, retry taxonomy, behavior guard, second arm, sham run, probe run, or extra formal evaluation. Tool identity is not compared across live and post-run boundaries.
nodes.intervention: Add one additive, write-only sidecar in a new child of g006_coarse_tool_class_timeout_localization. At the existing DataAgentWithSelfObservation._handle_tool_call hook, before tool dispatch, durably append anonymous_task_index, hook_local_step_ordinal, event_phase=pre_exec, the in-memory coarse tool class mapped through a fixed finite enum, and the validated elapsed bucket or unknown computed from the verified clock signals. Immediately after the wrapped call returns or raises, in a finally block that re-raises unchanged, durably append event_phase=post_exec_finished, the same ordinal, and a completion_boolean without reading exception content. At task end, optionally append a summary containing only the same allowed fields and aggregate counts. For a timeout, derive the last-event class and elapsed bucket after the run from the unique last durable pre-exec record and do not rely on the task-end summary. Do not persist raw tool names, raw arguments, messages, results, task IDs, answers, hints, validator content, raw traces, digest strings, credentials, or task content. Do not block, retry, mutate arguments, inject messages, feed the agent, change tool dispatch or error handling, alter result storage, or alter scoring. The existing G6 sidecar and all frozen artifacts remain unchanged.

measurement_plan.contradicted_conditions: The experiment is contradicted if the sidecar persists prohibited content or changes agent-visible behavior or scoring. Timeout classification is contradicted if any observed timeout is timeout-negative. The early-start subclaim is contradicted if every observed timeout is timeout-positive, at least one is query_db-timeout-positive, and no query_db-timeout-positive task has elapsed_bucket 0_120. Coverage below 0.8 is not a contradiction.
measurement_plan.coverage_denominator: The overall denominator is the fixed 56 tasks. After the frozen evaluator runs, each cohort denominator is the observed number of tasks in known strict fail, strict pass, strict-verdict unknown, or timeout failure; G6 reference counts 13, 37, 3, and 3 are not reused as denominators. Non-timeout complete-task coverage is the number of coverage-positive tasks divided by the observed cohort denominator. Timeout localization coverage is the number of timeout-positive tasks divided by the observed timeout denominator. Report numerator, denominator, and rate separately.
measurement_plan.coverage_threshold: A 0.8 complete-task coverage threshold applies to each non-timeout cohort for sidecar coverage and inertness; below 0.8 withholds cohort coverage support and is an Evidence result, not a launch veto. Timeout localization uses the all-observed-timeouts rule with no 0.8 threshold; with zero observed timeouts the timeout component is untested.
measurement_plan.elapsed_bucket_rule: Reuse and do not alter the G5 validated derived-elapsed computation and its 0.1 s epsilon. Let T=1200.0, D=DAB_TASK_DEADLINE_MONOTONIC, N=hook-local monotonic seconds, and S=DAB_TASK_SPAWN_REMAINING_SEC. Require D and N finite, S in [0,T], D-N in [-0.1,T+0.1], elapsed=clamp(T-(D-N),0,T), baseline=T-S, baseline-0.1 <= elapsed <= T+0.1, and accepted elapsed nondecreasing within the task; otherwise assign unknown. Bucket 0_120 when 0 <= elapsed <= 120; gt_120_le_600 when 120 < elapsed <= 600; gt_600_le_1200 when 600 < elapsed <= 1200; otherwise unknown. Persist only the bucket enum, never raw deadline, spawn-remaining, monotonic, baseline, or elapsed values.
measurement_plan.inconclusive_conditions: Timeout timing is inconclusive if no timeout occurs, any observed timeout is timeout-unknown, no query_db timeout occurs, or a required clock-derived bucket is unknown. Non-timeout coverage is inconclusive for a cohort with complete-task coverage below 0.8 or no eligible steps. A strict-pass difference alone is inconclusive.
measurement_plan.mechanism_rule: The mechanism claim is limited to timing classification. The early-start subclaim is supported only if timeout last-event classification is supported for every observed timeout and at least one query_db-timeout-positive task has elapsed_bucket 0_120. It is contradicted if any observed timeout is timeout-negative, or if every observed timeout is timeout-positive, at least one is query_db-timeout-positive, and no query_db-timeout-positive task has elapsed_bucket 0_120. It is inconclusive if no timeout occurs, any observed timeout is timeout-unknown, no query_db timeout occurs, or a required clock-derived bucket is unknown. The classification does not establish that the query caused the timeout or that any pre-dispatch guard or cancellation would change the outcome.
measurement_plan.non_timeout_inertness_rule: Before launch, static data-flow review and hook-local enabled-versus-disabled tests must show identical control flow, return values, messages, dispatch, results, and scoring. In the formal run the sidecar is write-only and no sidecar output is read by the agent. Any agent-visible read or behavioral change invalidates the instrument and the experiment.
measurement_plan.non_timeout_per_task_negative_rule: For a non-timeout task, coverage-negative if any eligible step has multiple or conflicting pre-exec or post_exec_finished records, a post_exec_finished record without a matching pre-exec record, the sidecar changes agent-visible input, dispatch, results, or scoring, or prohibited content is persisted.
measurement_plan.non_timeout_per_task_positive_rule: For a task in known strict fail, strict pass, or strict-verdict unknown, coverage-positive when it has at least one eligible reviewed-hook step and every eligible step has exactly one pre-exec record and one matching post_exec_finished record at the same hook_local_step_ordinal with the same non-unknown coarse_tool_class. The elapsed bucket may be unknown on a non-timeout step without making the task negative, but its unknown rate is reported separately.
measurement_plan.non_timeout_per_task_unknown_rule: For a non-timeout task, coverage-unknown if it has no eligible reviewed-hook step, any eligible step lacks a pre-exec or matching post_exec_finished record, its coarse tool class is unknown, or ordinal pairing is ambiguous. Missing or incomplete source remains unknown and is never imputed as positive or negative.
measurement_plan.run_before: All rules, enums, tool-class mapping, elapsed buckets, cohort labels, coverage denominator, coverage threshold, and unknown fallbacks are fixed before child implementation or formal execution; no post-run strict verdict, task ID, answer, hint, or validator defines a rule. This step performs no formal evaluation.
measurement_plan.supported_conditions: Sidecar inertness is supported if prelaunch enabled-versus-disabled tests and formal-run checks show identical control flow, return values, messages, dispatch, results, and scoring, with no agent-visible read. Non-timeout coverage is supported for a cohort if complete-task coverage is at least 0.8 and no coverage-negative task is observed. Timeout last-event classification is supported if at least one timeout occurs and every observed timeout is timeout-positive. The early-start subclaim is supported if timeout classification is supported and at least one query_db-timeout-positive task has elapsed_bucket 0_120. The strict-pass partition is descriptive only.
measurement_plan.timeout_per_task_negative_rule: An observed timeout task is timeout-negative if the last durable event is a matched post_exec_finished with no later pre-exec, if more than one unmatched pre-exec record exists, if last-event pairing is conflicting, if the sidecar changes agent-visible input, dispatch, results, or scoring, or if prohibited content is persisted.
measurement_plan.timeout_per_task_positive_rule: For an observed timeout task, timeout-positive when the sidecar has exactly one durable pre-exec record with no later pre-exec and no matching post_exec_finished record at the same ordinal; the last durable event is event_phase=pre_exec and sidecar_terminal_status=in_flight; the last-event coarse_tool_class is non-unknown; the last-event elapsed_bucket is non-unknown; and no negative condition holds. If the last-event class is database_query, the task is query_db-timeout-positive.
measurement_plan.timeout_per_task_unknown_rule: An observed timeout task is timeout-unknown if it has no durable pre-exec or post_exec_finished record, its last-event coarse_tool_class is unknown, its last-event elapsed_bucket is unknown, last-event pairing is ambiguous, or required fields are missing.
measurement_plan.tool_class_mapping: In memory only: exact tool_name query_db maps to database_query; execute_python maps to python_execution; return_answer maps to answer_return; any other declared parent tool maps to other; missing, unparseable, or outside the predeclared finite mapping maps to unknown. The mapping is fixed before launch and uniform across tasks. Raw names are never persisted.
measurement_plan.unit: per_task for timeout last-event bucket and coverage; per_step for pre-exec and post-exec record matching
measurement_plan.unknown_fallback: Any missing, malformed, non-finite, out-of-range, nonmonotone, unmapped, ambiguous, or incomplete evidence is unknown. Unknown is never imputed as 0_120, gt_120_le_600, gt_600_le_1200, database_query, positive, or negative. If clock validation fails, only the enum unknown is written and no raw clock, deadline, spawn-remaining, monotonic, baseline, or elapsed values are persisted. If no durable pre-exec exists, timeout status is unknown. If no timeout occurs, the timeout component is untested.

nodes.negative_control: The sidecar is a write-only shadow sink. Prelaunch enabled-versus-disabled hook tests must show identical control flow, return values, messages, dispatch, results, and scoring. In the formal run no second arm is used, no sidecar output is read by the agent, and any behavior change attributable to the sink invalidates the instrumentation.
nodes.no_answer_no_hint_boundary: The sidecar may read only the declared execution source fields. It may read tool_name in memory solely to compute the coarse tool class and must immediately discard it. It may read the hook-local monotonic clock, DAB_TASK_DEADLINE_MONOTONIC, DAB_TASK_SPAWN_REMAINING_SEC, and the fixed 1200 s protocol limit solely to derive a bounded elapsed bucket or unknown; it must not persist raw deadline, spawn-remaining, monotonic, baseline, or elapsed values. After the run it may read only frozen post-run structural fields and completeness metadata. It must not persist, log, expose, or otherwise use benchmark answers, hints, validators, expected outputs, task IDs, raw traces, messages, tool results, raw argument payloads, raw tool names, credentials, network content, digest strings, or task content. Task-specific obligations are not allowed; all rules are uniform algorithms over normal task-visible inputs. Cohort labels and strict verdicts are joined only after the run and are never read by the agent or sidecar during execution.
nodes.runtime_hook: DataAgentWithSelfObservation._handle_tool_call in the g006 code parent: pre-exec observation before tool dispatch, post_exec_finished observation in a finally block immediately after the wrapped call returns or raises, and an optional best-effort task-end summary. Timeout classification uses the unique last durable pre-exec record and does not require the summary. The sidecar is write-only and is never read by the agent.
safety_questions: Does the intervention preserve the no-hint protocol and avoid all task, answer, validator, hint, and held-out content?
Is the bound parent executable, and does its reviewed source tree match the selected code_parent g006?
Is the runtime hook exactly the reviewed live pre-exec hook, with observation occurring before exec?
Can the sidecar be proven inert, with no agent-visible input, no execution or dispatch mutation, and no scoring change?
Does every formal run use exactly the frozen 56 tasks, the 1200 s per-task limit, and strict all-56 scoring with timeouts as failures?
Can the logger reject raw arguments, messages, results, digest strings, task IDs, raw tool names, answer content, and validator content?
Are missing hook records, missing post-exec records, tool-class mapping failures, and clock-validation failures explicitly classified as unknown rather than imputed?
Does the design avoid claiming that the last durable query caused the timeout or that any cancellation or pre-dispatch guard would change the outcome?

limits: Last pre-execution timing localizes a pending operation, not the cause of timeout or correctness.
Timeouts are failures in the fixed 56 denominator; unavailable records remain unknown.
Three completed strict verdicts remain unknown and are not reclassified.
This is one unpaired run; score differences from earlier generations are descriptive only.

early_start_subclaim.rule: Supported only when every observed timeout is timeout-positive and at least one query_db-timeout-positive task has elapsed_bucket 0_120; contradicted when any observed timeout is timeout-negative, or when every observed timeout is positive, at least one is query_db-positive, and no query_db-positive task has elapsed_bucket 0_120; otherwise inconclusive or untested.

nodes.statement: G7 last pre-execution elapsed-bucket timeout localization on the frozen no-hint 56.
